title: Google Tests Next-Generation Gemini 4 Carbon Version, Code Capabilities Match Top Competitors
excerpt: As Google prepares to launch its next-generation Gemini 4 "Argon" model, internal teams have begun intensive testing of a follow-up iteration codenamed "Carbon.
content_html:
As Google prepares to launch its next-generation Gemini 4 "Argon" model, internal teams have begun intensive testing of a follow-up iteration codenamed "Carbon." The model has already been integrated into the internal code platform, aiming to further narrow the technological gap with industry-leading competitors.

Outstanding Performance in Complex Logical Tasks

According to internal documents and employee feedback, the new Carbon version performs exceptionally well in code generation and complex long-term tasks. Its preliminary test results are already approaching those of the strongest competing models. As Google continues to conduct in-depth testing of multiple derivative versions, the pace of technological advancement in its large model matrix is accelerating comprehensively.

Internal Codename and Final Name Are Independent

Notably, internal codenames of tech company products are usually not related to their officially released names. For example, the previously announced model had an internal codename of "Barium-B," so it remains uncertain whether Carbon will debut as an independent new model or be released as a regular version.
